**HTTP stream**: the server responds with Content-Type: text/event-stream and writes events
   as plain text.
Browsers can't set custom headers through EventSource.
**Event format**: each event uses fields like data:, event:, id:, and retry:.

to avoid slow clients blocking the broadcast.

**Heartbeat comments**: lines that start with : keep the connection open through proxies.
You need a simpler alternative to WebSockets for one-way streaming.
SSE is simpler for server-to-client push.
Set Cache-Control: no-cache and Connection: keep-alive to prevent buffering.

Forgetting to call Flush() after each event.

Server-Sent Events provide a lightweight, uni-directional channel for pushing real-time updates
from server to client over HTTP.

Unlike WebSockets, SSE uses standard HTTP connections, requires no
protocol upgrade, and the browser's built-in EventSource API handles reconnection automatically.
You can't control proxy or load-balancer timeouts that may close idle connections.

**Reconnection**: the browser tracks the last event ID and resends it in the Last-Event-ID
   header when reconnecting.

Send heartbeat comments every 30 seconds to keep
connections open.
You need to push notifications, logs, or live metrics to browsers.

Use long timeouts, disable response buffering in nginx with proxy_buffering off;, and use Redis
Pub/Sub to share events across instances if clients may land on different backends.
Over HTTP/1.1, browsers allow about 6 connections per domain.
Maintain a map of subscribed channels.
Missing Cache-Control: no-cache, causing proxies to buffer events.
Use longer write timeouts than for standard REST endpoints.
The server is the only sender; clients only receive.

**Formato de evento**: cada evento usa campos como data:, event:, id: y retry:.

**Heartbeat comments**: las líneas que empiezan con : mantienen la conexión abierta a través
   de proxies.

**HTTP stream**: el servidor responde con Content-Type: text/event-stream y escribe eventos
   como texto plano.
Necesitás enviar notificaciones, logs o métricas en vivo a navegadores.
Sí, pero algunos proxies tienen timeouts cortos.
Enviar eventos sin IDs, perdiendo el replay al reconectar.

mantener conexiones abiertas.
